Andrew Giuliani, the son of Donald Trump’s former personal lawyer and ex-New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani, reimagined his election-denying father as a legal force to write home about when asked about his controversies on Tuesday.

“I think what Rudy Giuliani has done over the last six years will go down in history as one of the most important legal jobs that has ever been done by any attorney,” he told reporters outside the White House of his father, who received the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

Rudy Giuliani was awarded the nation’s highest civilian honor in a closed-door ceremony at the White House a little over one year after Trump issued him and other election-denying champions “full, complete and unconditional” pardons.

Giuliani, of course, spearheaded efforts to overturn the 2020 election in Trump’s favor, promoting conspiracy theories at a press conference outside a small landscaping business and rambling as hair dye appeared to drip down the side of his face at another.

Two former Georgia election workers won a $148 million defamation lawsuit judgment against him, before ultimately settling.

Here’s how Andrew Giuliani described his father’s work to reporters on Tuesday, “Watching him go and take on a case that might not have been winnable in the time frame that he had, but I think more and more people now see how important, how consequential it was to put the facts on the table.”

Critics on social media were quick to knock Giuliani over the praise, including political commentator Molly Ploofkins who simply wrote on X, “He was disbarred.”

“One of the most embarrassing and unethical misuses of the law that has ever been done,” Ornstein wrote of Giuliani.
